tested_scope: Bounded public-source audit of GitHub pull-request service objects and hidden refs as a default service-side freshness/rollback witness paired with repository Contents-API CAS publication. No PR was created and no quota-bearing feature was consumed.

public_sources.observation: GitHub creates up to two temporary read-only refs for an opened pull request. refs/pull/N/head points to the latest commit on the pull request head branch; refs/pull/N/merge is a simulated merge ref and automatically changes as head/base changes.

GitHub documents that once a pull request is opened it stores the changes remotely and an inactive pull request can be fetched by pull/ID/head. The refs/pull namespace is read-only to repository users.

The REST API exposes pull requests by pull_number and can list open/closed/all states, but the retrieved documentation does not specify a monotonic-generation/fencing contract for pull_number, id or node_id and does not expose an expected-prior-witness conditional write coupled to repository Contents publication.

GitHub Enterprise Server documentation says pull requests may need deletion before commits can be garbage-collected. This is evidence that PR references can retain commits in that product, but it is not generalized here to a GitHub.com lifetime or anti-rollback guarantee.

observed: Pull-request hidden refs are GitHub-managed and read-only to ordinary repository pushes.
The head hidden ref tracks the latest pull-request head commit rather than freezing the generation present when the PR was created.
Previously opened/inactive pull-request changes are documented as remotely stored/fetchable.
Pull-request creation/update and repository Contents publication are distinct API effects in the retrieved documentation.
inferred_and_scope_limited: Because the head ref moves and no atomic cross-object CAS is documented, a PR hidden ref cannot by itself serve as a deterministic monotonic anti-rollback witness for a Contents-CAS generation.
Enterprise Server garbage-collection retention behavior is not proof of GitHub.com permanent retention or monotonic freshness semantics.

A PR number/id may be durable object identity, but without a documented monotonic freshness comparison and atomic/reconcilable linkage to the accepted generation it does not close the Part106 residual child.

result.new_falsification: GitHub pull-request hidden refs improve server-side reachability and user-write isolation, but refs/pull/N/head is explicitly movable with the PR head branch, and the PR object/ref write is not documented as atomic with Contents-CAS publication. The resulting missing-witness/orphan-witness traces plus absent documented monotonic freshness semantics prevent treating PR identity/hidden refs as the default rollback fence.
result.minimal_unresolved_child: A GitHub-native service-side witness whose freshness is monotonic across repository history rollback, whose accepted generation cannot be silently rebound, and whose publication coupling is atomic or deterministically reconcilable without hosted coordination or finite quota.

zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.note: This leaf only audited public documentation and lightweight repository/service semantics; it does not accept pull requests as the coordination mechanism.

conflict_check: Only own role-local state plus public GitHub documentation were used. No O, other-worker, downstream, legacy, aggregate-ledger, other-role receipt/config, scheduler or protected-primary semantic input was consumed.
